One of, if not the best game I've ever played. Constantly getting updates and additions to the game. Patches to balance the game are frequent and this is one of the most balanced game. The game has a steep learning curve and takes a lot of practice to get good. The big issue I have with the game is the ranked system is way too dependent on wins and losses. It is also very position dependent (mid/carry) and doesn't do a good job of evaluating someone's actually gameplay and impact on the game. You can have multiple games in a row where you are clearly the best player in the lobby and you lose and get penalized with a loss of rank, forcing you to continue playing the same players/rank you are consistently better than. Solo queue in ranked is not very fun, lots of auto losses in the first 10 min due to someone feeding the game away. Would just ask for a more impact based ranked system instead of a win or loss based.

Dota 2 is the kind of game that makes me question my life choices every single time I hit that play button. The matchmaking feels like it has a personal grudge against me, teammates either go AFK, pick the most ridiculous heroes, or just decide it’s a good day to ruin my MMR. The game itself is ridiculously complicated too, like no matter how many hours I put in, there’s always some obscure mechanic or item interaction I had no idea even existed. It’s overwhelming, it’s punishing, and most of the time it feels like the game is laughing at me. And yet, here I am, still playing it. Because every once in a while, everything lines up. The perfect teamfight breaks out, the clutch save comes in at the right second, or I land that skillshot I had no business landing. Those rare moments feel so good they completely erase the memory of the ten painful games that came before. That’s the worst part of it all—no matter how angry or frustrated I get, Dota knows exactly how to reel me back in. This game is pure suffering wrapped in brilliance. I hate it, but I can’t put it down.
